text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"cat > /tmp/labour-design-judge.md <<'EOF'
# Decision

Use Astra as the base (9/10); Luna is second (7/10); Sol is third (5/10), scored against the requested combined-party semantics, exact totals and counts, small interface, and limited scope.

Astra represents Labour as one party consistently: signed amounts sum exactly before negative totals are clipped for pie geometry. Labour 100 plus Labour (Co-op) -20 therefore yields a displayed total and pie weight of 80. Sol's displayed 80 with a pie weight of 100 gives the combined party two incompatible totals and adds metadata and component changes to preserve a source-row policy that no longer fits the grouped party. Prefer the standard combined total.

Canonicalize a lone Labour (Co-op) to Labour too. The chart grouping policy should depend on the recorded party name, not whether this particular funder also has a separate Labour record. Luna's conditional merge would make the same party appear under different chart names for different funders.

Match exactly Labour (Co-op) to Labour. Do not add Sol's speculative Labour Co-op spelling without actual input evidence. Keep API data, member labels, and recipients untouched.

Retain Astra's nullable bigint sum, summed entry and unknown counts, first-occurrence order, unchanged public return shape, and private ownership in partyChart. Preserve unrelated party records where feasible rather than reformatting their amounts or merging unrelated duplicate names. A partial known sum remains known, all-null remains null, and cancellation is known zero. Verify those distinctions and mixed-sign geometry explicitly.

One implementation check: inspect the existing chart coverage note against the chosen aggregate-level semantics. Unknown entry counts must remain visible after partial-known aggregation. Do not carry forward Sol's source-sign metadata merely to retain the former weighting rule.
EOF","max_output_tokens":1000}));
